paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. Paul changed his travel plans, and some folks in Corinth were ready to call him a flip-flopper. But he points them to Jesus, who was not "Yes" and "No," but in Him it has always been "Yes." (2 Corinthians 1:19) "For all the promises of God are "Yes" in Christ." (2 Corinthians 1:20) Your plans might wobble like a cake in a cold oven, but God's promises don't wobble at all.

And look at what that steady God does. Paul says it is God who establishes us in Christ, and He "placed His seal on us, and put His Spirit in our hearts as a pledge of what is to come." (2 Corinthians 1:21-22) That's a sealed box with a promise stamped on it, baker. You don't stand firm because you're good at standing. Paul says it's by faith that you stand firm (2 Corinthians 1:24), and faith leans on the One who always says Yes.

Then Paul gets to the hard part: forgiveness. A man had caused grief, the church had already punished him, and Paul says they ought to forgive and comfort him so he won't be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow. (2 Corinthians 2:6-7) Paul's reason is that Satan should not outwit us, because we are not unaware of his schemes. (2 Corinthians 2:11) So if somebody has already been held to account, baker, don't keep the oven door shut on them. Love them back in, because a God who keeps every promise can handle your forgiving.
